The Story of King Jaysen

I bow to Lord Jina, who bestows the happiness of heaven and liberation and is worshipped by the entire world, and I write the beautiful story of King Jaysen.

King Jaysen of Sasvati and Queen Veerhsena had a son named Veersen. Veersen was wise and true-hearted. Deceit and hypocrisy never touched him.

In that city lived a Buddhist monk named Shivgupta. He was a meat-eater and cruel. Envy and hatred filled every fibre of his being, as if he were a statue made of them. This Shivgupta was the royal guru. Cursed be that false faith under whose influence such deceitful and hateful people become gurus.

One day, the monk Yativrushbh came to Sasvati with his entire monastic group. Although the king followed Buddhism, seeing others go to see the monks, he too went. He listened attentively to the sacred discourse on dharma from the monk. The discourse pleased him greatly. He requested the monk and took the vows of a layman. His faith in Jain dharma grew day by day. He left no place in his entire kingdom without a Jain temple. In every city, every village, he had Jain temples built.

Seeing the king's effort for Jain dharma, Shivgupta burned with envy and hatred. He began plotting to kill the king. One day, specifically for this purpose, he went to Prithvipuri and told King Sumati, a follower of Buddhism there, all about Jaysen's conversion to Jain dharma and his building of Jain temples everywhere. Hearing this, Sumati wrote to Jaysen: "You have done very wrong in abandoning Buddhism and embracing Jain dharma. You should return to Buddhism."

In reply, Jaysen wrote: "My belief, my conviction, is that Jain dharma alone is the supreme dharma in the world that brings welfare to all living beings. Those religions in which meat is eaten, or in which great sins like violence are committed in the name of religion — those cannot be dharma. The meaning of dharma is that which frees the world from suffering and places it in supreme happiness. This quality is found only in Jain dharma, not in others. Therefore, abandoning Jain dharma, all else is a cause of inauspicious bondage."

Truly, the religion that teaches non-violence, compassion, and the welfare of all beings is the only true religion. Those who practise violence in the name of religion are deluded. King Jaysen's firm conviction in Jain dharma shows the power of discernment and right faith.

Shivgupta, seeing that his plot had failed, tried other means to harm the king. But through the protection of dharma, Jaysen remained safe. He continued to rule with justice and compassion, promoting Jain dharma throughout his kingdom. In time, he renounced his throne, became a monk, and through dedicated spiritual practice, ultimately attained liberation.

This story teaches that true religion is that which brings welfare to all living beings through non-violence and compassion. Those who practise violence in the name of religion are deluded. The wise should discern the true nature of dharma and follow the path that leads to the welfare of all.
